No. They won't even let me back into the upper district.
It's fine. This is temporary. Once they sort out their mistake, I won't spend another day down here.
That's the price? You didn't try to squeeze a little extra out of me?
The label says what it costs. That's what I charge.
Hmph. So not everyone in the lower levels is a swindler.
You miscalculated. You undercharged me.
I didn't miscalculate.
...I haven't fallen so low that I need a pawnshop owner to pity me.
But since you insist, I'll take it. I'll remember this. Don't expect a thank-you.
That's all? In the upper district this would buy two portions.
This isn't the upper district.
I can see that. The goods are from the lower levels. The prices are upper-district.
What? You don't even have food? And you call this a shop?
Sold out today.
Unbelievable... Fine. I'll look somewhere else.
My name is Eleanor. My mother's name will probably be in the news soon.
A name doesn't change the price.
I didn't ask you to change it! ...Just remember to save me something fresh next time.
I can't believe I'm stuck here.
No word from my mother, and they won't let me go back up. Why is this happening to me?
*sighs* Do you have household goods?
What do you need?
Cups, something to clean with... and a lamp that doesn't need two taps before it turns on.
Looks like I'll be here for a while.
I found a half-decent room across from the ration station. Small, but at least it doesn't smell.
This cup has a chip in it.
That's why it's cheap. The intact ones are over there.
I was only asking. It's not as if I can't afford an intact one.
So which one do you want?
...The cheap one. The chip isn't on the drinking side.
My roommate says fix the door lock first, then think about curtains.
She's right.
She also says the bottle of perfume I brought would cover half a month's rent.
If it's genuine, it would.
You can tell? I thought you only knew scrap metal.
In this business, you have to know the expensive things too.
...Hmph.
Same price you quoted. Fine, I'll take these.
Cheaper again? Do you do this for every customer?
Get the room sorted first.
I don't need you fussing over me. ...I'll take the lamp.
The same goods cost more here than anywhere else?
This is my first time living in the lower levels. It doesn't mean I can't do arithmetic!
Forget it. I'll look around. There must be more than one shop down here.
The neighbours argue every night. It sounds like they're right next to my bed.
Saves you buying a radio.
...That joke was terrible.
I can't believe people down here live like this their whole lives.
Hey. Me again.
My funds are running low. They didn't let me bring much with me.
As soon as I get back up there, I can explain everything and clear our names. Then everything can go back to normal.
And I'll never have to eat nutrifruit for every meal again.
Anyway, I brought some of my own things to sell. Water, perfume, a few household items.
Put them on the counter.
Careful! The cap on that bottle is loose.
You're not keeping the perfume?
Down here, I don't need to smell like I'm going to a banquet.
Besides, I doubt I'll be invited to any more banquets.
*opens the cap and sniffs* Custom blend from an upper-district salon, more than half full. Original bottle. The cap's just loose.
...You can tell from one sniff?
You don't see bottles like this down here twice a year. See one once and you remember it.
I thought you'd treat it like ordinary perfume and give me some random price.
Random prices ruin my own reputation.
Then keep calculating. You're really going to price every single item?
Would you rather I price it by your family name?
Lately, people who price by my name won't offer a single credit.
No one else in your family can help?
I don't have any family left. Only my mother.
Less than I expected. But you explained each item.
Fine. That price.
What about the depreciation you mentioned? Did you forget halfway through?
I have a use for this lot.
It had better be true. I don't want to come back and see them still sitting here, as if waiting for me to pity them.
You know what it's worth. You also know I'm short on money.
...Fine. Today you caught me at a bad time.
Fine, I'll take them. If you won't buy, someone else will.
There's also this. My mother gave it to me.
Selling that too?
...Ask me for a price first. I haven't decided.
Then put it away. Take it out when you've decided.
Aren't you afraid I'll sell it somewhere else?
It's yours.
...All right. I'm not selling this one today.
Hello there. You know Eleanor, don't you? I'm her... uncle.
We prepared a little gift for her. Only the best from the upper district.
But I can't find her anywhere.
An uncle who can't find his own niece?
Young people get upset and hide. I hear she comes here often.
Next time she visits, could you give this to her?
Make sure it reaches her hands. Not yours. Hers.
What's inside?
I told you. The best the upper district has to offer. She'll understand the moment she sees it.
If anyone asks, you never saw me.
Oh, and keep Security out of this. It's a family matter.
Good. Put it in her hands, not yours. I'll know.
Hello, shopkeeper. You reported stolen goods?
I didn't steal it! I have the receipt right here.
Then why did you report it as stolen?
Filing a false theft report is a crime. Come along quietly.
You run a shop, boss. Mind your own counter.
Someone tampered with my counter. That makes it my business.
*tells her about the man claiming to be her uncle*
My uncle? I don't have an uncle.
I told you. Apart from my mother, I don't have any family left.
That crate was reported stolen. I called Security. The person who filed the report was him.
He left me a crate? One that was reported stolen?
They wanted me arrested. Just like my mother.
The crate was reported stolen. It's in my storeroom now. Don't touch it.
A 'gift' that was reported stolen... They wanted me arrested. Just like my mother.
I didn't take it. He couldn't explain where it came from.
...Thank you for telling me.
If anyone else claims to be my family, throw him out.
My mother is already locked up. Isn't that enough for them?
I... I need some time to think.
Before all this, if someone sent me a crate like that, I wouldn't even check the label. I'd just open it.
And now?
Now I know nothing in the lower levels comes free. Nothing in the upper district either.
But you warned me. Please take something. It's the last thing I brought from home.
I'll come back when I've sorted out my thoughts.
I can't take it anymore.
My money's gone. Last night someone broke in and took what little I had left.
Only this locket survived because I was wearing it.
Are you hurt?
I wasn't there. My roommate went to ask around. I haven't heard from her since.
The verdict came down too. They found my mother guilty.
I don't know what to do. I'll be stuck down here forever, and my mother will rot in that cell.
I kept thinking about how I'd explain to her that I sold everything we brought from home.
Now... I don't even have the chance to explain.
I can't believe I've sunk low enough to ask this.
But could you spare some food? Anything edible. Please.
Thank you. I won't forget this.
That's enough. Really. Don't bring out any more.
Take an extra portion. For your roommate.
...She split her own dinner with me yesterday.
The first day I came here, I called you frogs in a well. I said people down here live like this their whole lives.
I remember.
Couldn't you just say you don't remember?
...I'm sorry. Those things I said were wrong.
I don't have any food today either.
...I saw the shelves. You don't have to explain.
If you ever get more stock, could you save me a little? Just a little.
...I understand. You run a shop, not a charity.
When I have money, I'll buy at full price.
Don't tell anyone about today.
Which part?
Me begging you for food. And me apologising.
Understood.
Especially the second part!
Don't tell anyone I came here to beg today.
I won't.
Thank you. There aren't many things I can still decide for myself. Let me keep this one.
Don't move! That crate was reported stolen.
What? It's not mine! I've never seen it before!
Like mother, like daughter. Come with us.
Please, someone set me up! Shopkeeper, tell them!
Did you sort it out with them?
They rechecked the theft report.
I said it over and over in there. The crate wasn't mine.
One of the officers laughed. He said my mother said the same thing.
You're out.
Yes. But she's still in there.
I shouldn't have handed it to you directly.
You were tricked too. ...But next time, ask me first. All right?
You knew it was reported stolen?
I knew. I messed up.
Then don't act as if getting me out makes it never happen.
I'll write down what you spent on me. I'll pay back every credit.
Eat something first.
...You still have food here?
If I have it, I'll give it to you. If not, we'll think of something together.
...All right.
Hey! I'm back!
After last time, I figured things out. Life goes on. Besides, I'm almost used to the stench.
First priority: survival. So I went scavenging at the dump.
My roommate gave me a crash course in scavenging. I have to admit, there's a real community spirit down here.
Anyway, come look at what I found! ...Don't laugh.
I haven't said anything.
Your face already did.
I think this one's usable. That one's old, but the inside is fine.
You're right about this one.
You don't have to say every piece is good just to make me feel better.
Then this one gets a lower price. It's broken here.
...So that wasn't dirt? I spent ages wiping it.
You did a good job.
That one was just to make me feel better.
Good. You take the goods, I take the credits.
This is much better than standing here waiting for you to pity me.
You paid too much.
This lot will sell well.
Then you'll have to tell me what it's normally worth. I have to learn.
Is that price because the goods aren't worth much, or because you think I can only sell to you?
It's fine. I'll remember what you don't buy and bring something else next time.
I've been thinking about what to do next.
I'm sure someone in the upper district set up my mother. I can't go up there and ask around, but a private investigator can.
A reliable one costs eight hundred credits.
That's not a small amount.
I know. So I'll keep scavenging and sell what I find to you.
Give me a fair price, all right? Every credit gets me closer.
I've asked other buyers too, and I took some short work cleaning grow tanks. I can't rely on your shop alone.
Write down what you earned today.
Already did. Don't think you're the only one on this station who can keep accounts.
Hey, me again. Don't look at the goods first today.
How am I supposed to buy without looking?
I'll quote first. Then you tell me what I got wrong.
Fine.
This casing is dented, but the inside's fine, so normal price. This one looks new, but the connector's rusted, so lower it. This one... I'm not sure.
Two right, one unsure. Last time's lesson wasn't wasted.
You didn't charge tuition. It doesn't count as a lesson.
Then I'll start charging next time.
You can't charge for lessons already given!
At the dump today, someone tried to trade me a bag of broken parts for my stuff. Said I clearly didn't know the market.
Did you trade?
Of course not! I told him to take it to the pawnshop and let the owner decide what it's worth.
The moment he heard it was your shop, he turned around and left faster than I did.
I didn't expect your shop's name to carry more weight than my family name down here.
It only works when I'm buying scrap.
Still better than my name. My name can't even buy scrap now.
He said he'd never heard of any pawnshop, muttered something, and left.
At least I didn't get fooled. That's the important part.
Add today's sale, and we're one step closer to eight hundred.
Did you set aside food money?
I did. Nutrifruit doesn't taste like punishment every meal now.
...Sometimes it still does.
You know, I used to think helping someone meant throwing a fortune at them.
Now I know that someone honestly buying what I scavenged at a fair price is enough to keep me going.
Don't tell me again that this is just what the lower levels pay. I've asked other buyers.
Things are worth what they're worth. They don't become worth less because I'm in a hurry.
Wait. Don't count this piece of material with the rest.
Valuable?
...It's for you.
You still need money for the investigator.
I know. This doesn't come out of that.
Last time you were buying, you looked at this kind of material a little longer. I found some, so I kept it.
You noticed that?
I don't just stand here waiting to count your money.
Don't get the wrong idea. I just have good eyes.
Then I'll take it.
Good. When you use it, don't tell people you just picked it up somewhere.
...Even though I did.
This is something I wanted to give you. If you insist on paying, fine.
But you should know, this time I'm not asking you for help.
Keep it and sell it.
Fine. Next time I'll pick something you can't find an excuse to refuse.
My roommate asked how I knew you'd be open today.
What did you say?
I said anyone running a proper business opens on time.
Did she believe you?
She asked why I don't go to another shop.
And then?
Then I told her to mind her own radio and stop playing it at midnight.
What are you laughing at? She really is loud!
I'll slowly pay back what you've done for me.
You don't have to say that every time you come.
Then this is the last time I'll say it. From now on, watch what I do.
So this is the shop Eleanor never stops talking about?
She's not here today.
I know. I picked a time when she wouldn't be.
Buying or selling?
Selling. *sets a bracelet on the counter* I'll name the price. You decide what to pay.
She says you have a sharp eye. I'd like to see how sharp.
You priced it too low. Upper-district handmade work. The clasp was replaced, but it doesn't hurt the value.
...You can tell the clasp was replaced?
The new clasp is brighter than the band.
Fine. She wasn't exaggerating.
You took it without arguing.
She said you never take advantage of people. I suppose it depends on whose advantage it is.
You won't buy it? Fine. At least you didn't pretend to know.
She used to buy things based only on whether she liked the look. She never asked the price.
Now she asks more questions than anyone.
She told me. She said when you buy goods, you put the fault on the item, not the person.
Her exact words?
Her exact words were much ruder. I picked the part I could repeat.
I can find her a job up there. A place to live too.
Then you should tell her.
I did. She has one condition: stop bringing up her mother's case in public. She won't agree.
Then she's already given you her answer.
She keeps saying 'there are people down here too.' I thought she was just being stubborn.
...What exactly have you people done to her?
Nutrifruit.
*snorts* ...No wonder she says you're infuriating.
If she asks, tell her I came to sell something.
I'll tell her everything you said.
...Suit yourself. Just don't make me sound better than I was.
Did Lydia come by?
She did. Sold a bracelet, and mentioned she could find you a job up there.
With conditions, I assume.
Yes.
I turned her down. Not because the job was bad.
I can't live in a house someone else gives me, learn to keep my mouth shut, and pretend my mother doesn't exist.
...What else did she say?
That you're infuriating.
She got that one right.
She also asked whether you were only interested because I used to have money, waiting for the day I recover so you can cash in.
What did you say?
I said that when everyone else changed their expression the moment they heard my name, you were still looking down at the goods.
On my poorest days, you didn't suddenly get better at arithmetic.
I said you've done things that made me furious. But you came back and made them right.
I know what happened better than she does. She doesn't get to decide for me.
I said I'd judge for myself. ...If you really are waiting for me to recover before you start offering fair prices, you'd better stop waiting.
You don't have to vouch for my shop.
Who's vouching for you? I have confidence in my own judgement.
She said I never used to admit I'd misjudged someone.
And now?
Now I do. For example, I used to think everyone down here was the same.
Don't get smug. I'm not right about people every time either.
I know.
...You answered that very quickly.
By the way. Did she also praise your eye for goods?
Something like that.
She praises everyone like that. Don't take it seriously.
...And don't talk to her too long. That mouth of hers could talk anyone in circles.
I've sold out for today. Can I stay here a little longer?
Only when there are no customers.
Fine. It's not as if I'm here to keep you from making money.
If today's batch sells, it should be enough.
Price the goods first. Don't start from the number you want.
I know, I know. I can already say that line for you.
I know exactly how much is missing. If it's not enough, I'll make another run to the dump tomorrow.
There. I think the money should be enough.
Count it again.
I've counted it three times! Eight hundred. Not a credit short.
Before, a number like that was just a line on a bill. I'd skim past it without even looking.
Now I can tell you where every single credit came from.
Including the scrap you spent ages wiping?
The material from that later sold too. Stop calling it scrap.
The investigator agreed to start with my mother's work records, not go straight to the company.
Don't hand him all the originals.
I kept copies, and I wrote down every meeting time.
When does he start?
Tomorrow.
Thank you. I'm going to find out who did this to my mother.
...Today I was going to say I finally don't have to keep running to your shop.
You're not coming anymore?
I didn't say that. Until it's cleared up, I still have to eat.
Then come as usual.
...Yeah.
I can pay. But from now on, you listen to me.
Put the business terms in writing. Whether I take the loan is my decision.
Not just business.
Then no loan.
My mother never taught me to pay my debts with myself. That's not how things work down here either.
The money's done. I sold the rest of the goods to another buyer and took an advance on some short work.
What was their price like?
Not great. I'll be working extra days. But I'll manage.
Don't look at me like that. I said I'd find a way.
The last part of the shortfall, I was planning to cover with the locket.
It's been hanging on me doing nothing. Now I want it to help me find my mother.
You've thought it through?
I have. Price it like anything else.
Hey. The investigator found something.
First tell me: was he followed?
He says no. We changed the handoff point, and I didn't come straight here.
It's a data drive, hidden in my mother's old lab at the hydroponics farm.
Did he open it?
It has a password. He couldn't. But I know it. Mom always used my birthday.
I told her so many times that it wasn't safe. She said she was afraid she'd forget it one day when she was busy.
Did she ever forget?
Not once.
I can't wait any longer. Let's open it here.
*stares at the screen*
This is... genetic research. About nutrifruit.
She found a way to make ordinary nutrifruit produce seeds again.
Plant it once, and you can keep your own seed.
Yes. With this data, any decent biohacker could modify it.
No one would have to buy seeds from Pastel again. It would cost Pastel a fortune.
That's why they went after her.
There are work records too. She wrote that someone demanded she stop the experiment. Not long after, her access was revoked.
The embezzlement charge was fabricated. All of it. The representative of Pastel's station office planned the whole thing.
That alone won't make a court release her.
I know. But at least now I know what she was doing, and what they were afraid of.
Don't rush to take it out.
I know. My mother is still in their hands.
I... I need some time to think about what to do.
Leave it with me. No one takes it without asking you first.
You know this isn't ordinary stored goods?
I know. That's why I'm telling you first.
...Good. I'll remember what you said.
People come and go here every day. It'll be safer with you.
All right. We agree on who it goes to first. No changing our minds at the last minute.
This is too big. I can't be involved anymore.
...I understand. I'll take the drive. Please don't tell anyone what I said today.
That crate last time. Remember me?
Out already?
Someone handled the paperwork. See? Some things aren't as hard as you think.
Boss, I have a message. About Eleanor and the research disk she has.
We know you've been dealing with Eleanor. We also know about the drive.
Who are you passing the message for?
She's seen what's on it. She knows who.
Tell her to give it back, or her mother dies.
If she hands it over, we release her mother. She'll be exiled to the lower levels, but she'll live.
Why should I believe you?
It doesn't matter whether you believe me. She just has to.
If you get her to return it, you'll earn three hundred credits.
You run a pawnshop. Why make this complicated?
Who handles the release? When can she see her mother?
Someone will handle it. Not your concern.
You really plan to see this through for her? ...Don't take too long.
Boss, you'd better think carefully. Your name will be in the record too.
Then write it all down. Don't just write hers.
Message delivered. Tell her to come talk when she's decided.
*tells her about their offer to release her mother*
If I return the drive, they'll let her go?
Exiled down here... but alive.
He also said I'd get three hundred when it's done.
...You told me even that.
You should know all of it.
Thank you.
But if I publish it, they'll kill her. And then no one would need Pastel's seeds anymore.
I want her to live. I can't pretend to be brave about that.
You don't have to pretend.
But the research is real. You saw it.
Even if I secretly keep a copy and hand it back, they'd still find a way to hurt her.
So if we want to keep the research, we have to make sure they can't reach her first.
I don't know what to do. If it were you, what would you do?
There's a way. Apply to have her moved into supervised protective custody, then reopen the review of her case.
The frame-up and the threat records prove she's in danger now. The research explains why they're doing this.
I'll prepare her identity papers and medical history. I know what medication she used to take.
I don't have a channel that can get her out. My word alone isn't enough.
Then we negotiate their release terms first. I can't gamble with my mother's life.
If someone takes over her protection, I want to know who's responsible and when I can see her.
Verify what can be verified first. Publishing without protection means gambling with her life.
And don't go see that enforcer alone.
Afraid I'll get hurt?
I'm already waiting for one person to come out of there. I don't want to wait for another.
Bring your mother back first. Return the research.
You're right. She's my only family.
But I want to see them release her myself. Not send her from one locked door into another.
Secure the transfer and protection first. Once she's safe, we decide who gets the research.
All right. I'll organise her records. Tell me what you need, and don't do everything alone and only tell me afterward.
If we publish, everyone will know what they did. But I can't promise your mother will live.
I know they're not bluffing.
Let me think again. I can't hide it just because I'm afraid, and I can't pretend I'm the only one who's afraid.
I've decided.
This matters more than either of us. Mom would want everyone to have it.
You're not waiting for protection?
No. I'm taking it to a lower-level newspaper today.
But don't tell me that means she'll be safe. We both know it doesn't.
I've handed in Mother's protection paperwork. Checked the medication section again.
The application is in too. We're waiting for a reply.
You didn't tell me 'it's already fine.'
I can't say that yet.
That's better, actually. People used to tell me 'don't worry' every time they saw me, and then I never saw them again.
Are you still taking short work tonight?
Yes. Waiting for news doesn't feed anyone.
I told my roommate that if anyone asks where my mother lives, not to say a word.
What did she say?
She said I've learned this late.
Your name is on the application too.
Yeah.
I checked your shop address twice.
Afraid you'd write it wrong?
Afraid that if something happens, I wouldn't be able to find you.
I'm right here.
I know. That's why I dared to take it this far.

The safety review for the person concerned has been accepted. Transfer to temporary protective custody approved; family may visit after verification. This measure does not mean the original case is dismissed.
I... I can see her?
Go to the place and time written there. Verify first, then see her.
All right. I'm going now.
If it's real, I'll come back and tell you. In person.
They agreed to arrange the release and the handover on the same day.
Verify the person and the paperwork first. Don't just trust the messenger.
I want my mother to confirm it herself. Someone else reading a line for her doesn't count.
What about a copy of the research?
No copy. If I'm using it to buy her life, I can't gamble on them not finding out.
You've thought it through?
I have. If there's another way later, that's for later.
Today, I just want to see her.
Still no confirmation that she can be released, right?
No. We can keep applying, or switch to the exchange.
I don't want to treat 'processing' as if she's already safe. Get her out first.
Hey! My mother is free!
You saw her yourself?
Myself! The first thing she asked was whether I'd been skipping meals again.
Sounds like she knows exactly who you are.
She was exiled to the lower levels. She can't go back to her old farm.
But we're together again. Tonight, I know where she's sleeping.
I've seen Mother! She's been moved out, someone's looking after her, and visits are registered.
Does she know what happens next?
She does. The research, the threat, and what we plan to publish. I told her everything.
She said to let the protection staff confirm the arrangements first, then send the material out.
She's more careful than you.
She said I'm reckless enough for both of us. Someone in the family has to ask more questions.
I had so many things prepared. I wanted to ask how she ate in there, why she didn't tell me sooner, whether anyone hurt her.
Did you ask?
Not a single one. I just called her 'Mom'.
She said she heard me, and I didn't have to shout.
You can ask the rest slowly.
Yeah. Now we can take our time.
I used to think that as long as I could get back up there, everything would return to how it was.
But today, when I saw her, I didn't even think about the house up there.
What about a place to live?
We'll find something suitable down here first. My roommate said she'd help look, and I can keep working.
Come pick out whatever you need.
At full price. You've already helped us too much. I can't have you paying for everything from now on.
Understood.
But today, I want to thank you properly, once.
Not because of how much money you spent on me. Because when I said 'she's alive,' you didn't treat it as something unimportant.

The research on restoring nutrifruit seeds has been handed to independent researchers for verification. The representative of Pastel's station office is suspected of coercion and interference in the case and is now under investigation.
The person concerned is currently under registered protection. The original embezzlement case is still under review; the investigation result does not constitute a final ruling.

The registered protection arrangements have been confirmed. The family is permitted to register a residence in the lower levels and live together, and may carry on normal daily activities. Contact person and address are on file; contact must be maintained during the review of the original case.
Hello. Eleanor says that when you buy things here, the owner tells you the flaws first.
What else did she say?
That the owner isn't always good with words, but isn't a bad person.
That sounds like her.
I'd like to buy some household goods. There's still a lot missing where we live.
She didn't come with you?
She's working. Before she left, she told me not to grab everything just because it's cheap.
When I used to tell her that, she pretended not to hear.
She's very careful with money now.
She could always do arithmetic. She just never had to count for herself before.
She told me what you did for her.
She did plenty herself.
I know. But when she talks about herself, she says far less than when she talks about you.
Probably thinks there's nothing worth mentioning.
Or maybe she's waiting for me to ask.
The research was returned. Of course that doesn't sit well with me.
But don't let her think bringing me back is something she has to apologise for.
The material has been sent out. I'll keep cooperating with the review. The rest will take time, step by step.
You were right to get me transferred before publishing. The people with the least protection shouldn't always be the ones paying the price.
That's all. Don't refuse to take my money just because it's me.
You two even say the same thing.
In some ways, she really is like me.
When she talks about this place lately, it's not just about what she bought.
What else does she say?
You'll have to ask her yourself. I'm not going to finish her sentences for her.
Did my mother come by?
She did. Bought some things, paid for them.
Did you only talk about shopping?
No.
...I knew it.
She told me to ask you myself.
Then don't ask today!
I brought some goods. Not an excuse. They're actually sellable.
I didn't say it was an excuse.
You'd better not even think it.
My mother gets up earlier than I do now. Two days ago I woke up and found her sitting there repairing an old tray.
Can't sit still?
She says if her hands aren't doing something, she starts thinking about what happened in there.
I handed her the tools and sat with her for a while.
That's good.
Yeah. Nothing special. Just sat for a while.
I always thought that once she was out, I'd know what to do next.
And now you don't?
Work continues, the room needs tidying, meals have to be made. I know all that.
It's just... I don't need to invent a reason to come here so I can ask you for help.
You don't need a reason to come here.
You said that. Remember it.
I'll still come to sell goods. You don't have to ask me what happened every time.
As an ordinary customer?
As a regular. Ordinary customers don't know what you buy.
There's something we need to settle first. I haven't forgotten the crate from the man pretending to be my uncle.
I didn't expect you to.
You did make it right afterward. And you stopped making me guess what you knew and didn't know.
I'm willing to trust you again. But that doesn't mean what happened was right.
I know. From now on, if I know about a danger, I'll tell you first.
Remember what you said. Not just today.
I didn't bring any goods today.
And you're not short of anything?
No. Don't make excuses for me.
There's something I want to say clearly. Otherwise you'd probably keep pretending not to notice.
What is it?
I've been coming here... more often than when I had goods to sell.
I noticed.
Then why did you ask!
After my mother got out, I wondered whether I kept thinking about this place because you'd helped me so much.
And you figured it out?
When I think about you, it's not only about my mother.
I wonder whether you got anything good today, whether you let your lunch go cold again, whether you argued with another difficult customer.
None of that is written in the debt I owe you.
So?
So... I like you.
There. Your turn. And this time you don't get to change the subject with a price tag.
I like you too. It has nothing to do with where you used to live.
I know that. You've seen me at my worst.
And your worst temper.
You'll be seeing that often. You can still back out now.
I won't.
...Good.
Then from now on, I won't have to say I was 'just passing by.'
I want to know you better. But can we take it slowly?
Yes. I'm not asking you to sign a lifetime contract today.
Just don't pretend you didn't hear me.
I care about you. But not that way.
...I see.
You telling me directly is better than letting me guess.
You don't have to repay me for the help I gave you.
I know. I'm not trying to repay a debt.
I'll still come sell goods in a couple of days. Act normal then.
I said some harsh things before. I want to add one thing today.
Thank you for always treating me like someone who can do things for herself.
You always could.
Now I believe it. If you ever need me for something, you can come find me.
I saw a batch of goods you might want. I didn't agree to anything for you.
Why didn't you bring it directly?
You said it yourself: look at the goods first, then listen to the person.
I asked where it came from, and what's broken. When the person arrives, you look for yourself.
You know not to make decisions for me.
Of course. I just wanted you to know, this time I'm bringing you business.
Well? I picked well, didn't I?
You didn't hide the flaws. That's good.
I was asking about my eye, not my character!
Your eye is good too.
Not suitable? Then don't buy it. It's not as if you have to buy something just because I brought it.
Will you help me look next time?
Yes. But first I need to figure out where I went wrong this time.
My mother says my tone when bargaining sounds more and more like yours.
Does she think that's a good thing?
She says at least now I know what I'm talking about.
How did you answer?
I said the teacher is average. The student is the smart one.
So what does the teacher get?
A girlfriend this clever isn't enough?
Enough.
That was a quick answer.
Next time you could teach some other beginners.
Fine. First lesson: don't fall down in the same place twice.
Today I'm really here to buy something.
You sold something last time too.
Last time I also said a lot of things that weren't mine to decide for Eleanor.
Did you apologise to her?
I did. She said don't just apologise to the owner, as if she doesn't have a mouth of her own.
I saw her mother. Thinner than before. Still talks the same way, won't let anyone praise her too much.
They're settling in slowly.
Eleanor told me about recent events too. This time, I heard the whole story from beginning to end.
That bracelet. I had someone look at it when I got back. Your price was fairer than mine.
When I tell people about it, they don't believe there's a shopkeeper like that in the lower levels.
Before, when we picked gifts, we only worried they weren't expensive enough.
This time she told me to bring things that are actually useful, not turn a visit into an exhibition.
She's right.
She is. It's the tone that makes it hard to admit right away.
She told me you're together.
Do you have any conditions to raise?
No. It's just that when she said it, she had no intention of asking my opinion.
Word going around up there is that Eleanor has taken a liking to a pawnshop owner in the lower levels.
The rumour's correct.
I defended her a little. ...Don't thank me. I did it for her, not you.
She says you're a friend worth keeping. She rarely uses the word 'worth.'
So is she.
I'm learning to understand that again.
If suitable business comes up in the future, I'll have people come talk to you directly. You won't owe me a favour.
If the goods are right and the price is right, we'll talk.
No wonder she says that all the time now.
My mother found a place willing to let her help organise equipment. Not her old farm, but she wants to go.
Are you going too?
I'll help for a few days. I found steadier work myself too, so I won't have to rely only on scavenging.
It's not the life we had before, but it's our own.
I used to think this kind of work didn't count. Now I think being able to support a family on your own is already impressive.
Someone from the research side came to ask if we'd help organise the records my mother left behind.
Up there?
Some of the work is up there. It needs a separate work permit. It's not a return to our old life, and the case isn't closed.
My mother wants to keep doing research. I want to understand the parts I couldn't follow.
If you want to go, go.
Of course I'm going. I didn't come here today to ask for your permission.
Then you came to notify me?
I came to discuss how to arrange the time! Can't you let me finish a sentence?
I want to keep working, and I want to keep seeing you.
You don't have to turn down an opportunity for this shop.
I wasn't planning to turn it down. I wasn't planning to turn you down either.
Before, other people arranged my life for me. All I had to do was pick what I didn't like.
Now I choose for myself. Don't start deciding 'what's good for me' again.
Then we'll go with your arrangement. Tell me when you're busy.
You too. Stop saying the shop can't spare you and skipping proper meals.
I've thought about what happened last time. I want you to come here as more than a regular.
Are you sure? You're not going to make me guess again?
I'm sure.
...All right. I'll make time. You have to make time too.
I might not come as often in the future. But we can still help each other with business.
If I come across something suitable, I'll keep an eye out for you.
Thank you. If you need anything, don't forget to ask me.
Do you remember this?
That time you asked for a price and didn't sell it.
I told my mother I wanted to give it to you. She said it's mine, so I decide.
And this time it's not for sale?
No. You'd better have learned to tell the difference by now.
Then I'll keep it.
Don't put it with the goods on the counter. I'm not that generous.
It looks better on you. I'll take the thought.
...Fine. I'll wear it myself. It's not as if you won't see me again.
I originally wanted to give you that locket. In the end, I sold it to make up the money.
You don't need to find something else to replace it.
I know. I just wanted you to know that I thought about it.
Hey. Do you have time today?
Nobody's hurt?
No. My mother's fine, and I haven't lost my job.
You'll have to get used to it. Me coming here doesn't always mean something happened.
I'm getting used to it.
Then get used to it faster.
My mother keeps telling me to bring an extra portion of food.
For your roommate?
She has hers too. This one's for you.
How are you two doing now?
The room's still small, and we still have to count every credit. My mother has nightmares sometimes.
But when she wakes up, I'm right there, and I can answer her.
That's good.
Yeah. Not everything has come back. But we're not left with only what we lost.
The first time I came here, I said your shop wasn't much.
And now?
There's still plenty that needs fixing. Don't think that because I like you, I'll like that broken lamp too.
You're demanding.
You agreed to this. My temper isn't going to vanish just because we're together.
I remember.
Then let me stay here with you for a while today. If a customer comes, do your business.
And if no one comes?
Then talk to me.
About what?
Anything. Just don't start with 'how much money are you short?'
I used to think that once I went back up, I wouldn't need to keep in touch with people I met down here.
And now?
Now I know that sorting people by where they live is incredibly stupid.
I'll remember that.
You can remember it. Just don't recite it every time you see me.
Come find me when you need something. Or when you don't. Friends don't only count when someone's short of money.
Later, she sometimes came from work, sometimes after running errands with her mother. She still complained your lamp wasn't bright enough, still insisted every account be settled to the last credit.
Only now no one had to guess why she kept coming back to this pawnshop.
Before you left, you told her. She first asked whether everything on your journey was arranged, then went through every way of contacting you one by one.
She didn't say it would all be easy. You simply agreed that every step ahead would be explained to each other.
When Eleanor heard, she started asking everywhere for news of you. She remembered how you had verified every promise one by one, and knew that saying 'it'll be fine' was nowhere near enough.
Whether she can change the outcome depends on how much room the ending leaves. A completed romance does not erase the original punishment.
Later, she still came to this shop. No trade, no question waiting for an answer.
What she remembered about you wasn't only the ending, but also those first small accounts, every one calculated so clearly.
She rebuilt her life bit by bit. Sometimes she brought goods, sometimes she introduced business for acquaintances.
You never became lovers, but she would never again see the lower levels as merely a place she had to endure.
Her messages didn't always reach you. When she appeared, it wasn't always to talk about research or the Revolution.
Sometimes she only asked whether your shop was still open. She remembered that in this pawnshop, she could be just Eleanor.
She never came again. Everything you heard about her came from other customers.
The pawnshop's ledger recorded that income, but no column could record who had been missing from then on.
You still haven't fixed that lamp?
It still lights up.
My chipped cup still holds water too. But you clearly said you had intact ones!
Of course you remember that.
Naturally. How could I be careless about the first account I ever settled with you?
My mother made too much, so she told me to bring some over.
How is it always exactly one extra portion?
Do you want it or not?
I want it.
Then ask one fewer question that's hard for the cook to answer.
I knew that customer just now. He used to tell me not to associate with people down here.
He seemed happy enough to buy today.
I told him: if you want to buy something, follow the rules here. If you want to teach me how to pick a boyfriend, please leave.
What did he choose?
Buying. He isn't always that tactless.
Don't waive this one today. I got paid.
You don't have to prove you can afford it every time.
I know. I just want you to know, you're not the only one who can take care of someone.
Then charge it at full price.
Yeah. And after that, sit and talk with me for a while.
I sorted this batch. The faulty ones are together. Don't say I didn't warn you.
You're starting to sound like a veteran.
I always was. Don't bring up my first scavenging trip for the rest of my life.
Then can I bring up your first food shopping trip?
...Let's talk about today's prices first!
Let's not talk about all that today. Got anything new in the shop?
Goods, or news?
Goods. Preferably the kind I can find a few flaws in.
I've got plenty.
Good. Sounds like an ordinary trip to the shop.
The Nutrifruit research is with the newspaper. They say they'll have it checked before publishing it.
Did you tell them about your mother's situation?
I did. They agreed to include the threat, but they didn't promise they could get her out.
We'll keep asking about her.
Yeah. I left an address where they can find me.
You don't have to tell me we did the right thing.
I won't.
I just wanted someone to know that when I made the decision, I didn't forget her.

The secret behind Pastel's nutrifruit has leaked! A research paper reveals how ordinary nutrifruit can be made to produce seeds again. The same morning, the former head of the station's largest hydroponics farm, imprisoned for embezzlement, was found dead in her cell. Pastel has declined to comment.
Hey. It's me.
The morning the paper came out, they killed my mother.
...Are you sure?
I went to identify her. It wasn't a rumour.
They said it was a sudden illness. On the very morning the paper came out.
Eleanor...
Don't tell me she would have wanted this. I can't ask her anymore.
All right. I won't speak for her.
I know there were other ways. I know why I didn't choose them.
But knowing that doesn't make this any easier.
You don't have to decide anything today.
I want to stay here for a while. Don't ask me if I want a drink.
All right.
They only returned a few of Mother's things.
Is there anything you want to keep?
A list she wrote. All little things about the farm.
Which light was broken, what tools were missing, which grow tank needed checking again.
She was always thinking about it.
Yeah. Not every page was research that could change the whole station.
Most of the time, she was just busy with these things.
Keep it.
I will. This isn't for sale.
Thank you. I'll take the food.
Life has to go on. I know. Just not that fast.
I joined the Revolution.
Did they come to you?
They approached me. But in the end, I went to them myself.
They'll help me make Pastel pay, and they can keep me out of the company's reach. The research can keep spreading too.
Do you know what they want you to do?
I asked. I'm not going to agree to anything just because someone promises revenge.
You're leaving?
I won't stay in the same place. I can't come here on a fixed schedule anymore.
Don't turn every meeting into a message drop.
I won't use your shop as a contact point. You helped me. That doesn't mean you should carry every risk from now on.
But sometimes, I might still need someone to talk to like a normal person.
You know where this place is.
I know. I've always known.
All right, I need a weapon. What do you have?
Do you know how to use one?
Someone's teaching me. I'm not going to wave around something I can't use just to frighten people.
Check the condition first. Don't settle for a broken one.
This time I'll listen to you.
The money's enough. Don't waive this one for me.
Then I'll look elsewhere. I'm not in a hurry to take something more likely to hurt me.
Before, all I wanted was to go back to how things were.
Now I can't even say what I want to become.
Then at least don't take everyone's words as truth.
Yeah. Including yours.
Including mine.
I'm looking for Eleanor. But she said not to ask around about where she lives.
Then don't ask.
I'm not here to take her back. I know how awful that sounds right now.
I just want to explain what her mother did for my family before. Back then, I did nothing for her.
When she's willing to listen, tell her yourself.
All right. I'll wait until she's willing.
If she needs something normal that can be bought, I can help find it. I don't need to know where she goes.
I can pass that on.
I got Lydia's message.
Do you want to see her?
Later. I don't have the energy to teach everyone how to talk to me right now.
Then later.
I know there are things between us we never finished saying.
You don't have to finish them before you leave.
I care about you. That didn't disappear because something happened to my mother.
But I can't promise to come back on time, and I can't ask you to stop your life and wait for me.
Then don't promise something you can't do.
...All right. When I can come back, I will.
I'll remember this place. Not just the research and the investigator's money.
And remember the first time you turned your nose up at my cup?
That cup really did have a chip. I wasn't wrong about that.
I'm here for food for the road. We're leaving with the revolutionaries soon.
Still not nutrifruit?
I want it. Now when I see it, I feel like at least some things weren't for nothing.
Pick what you can carry.
Yeah. Charge me as usual.
I should go.
Take care of yourself.
You too. Don't take on every trouble that comes to your door.
Depends.
...Of course you'd say that.
Thank you again. For everything. I hope next time we can talk about something else.
Where's Mother's research disk?
I already handed it over. They promised to release her.
Did you confirm it?
Not yet.
Then what did you get?
Three hundred credits.
I asked you to keep it safe, not to decide what my mother is worth.
It might still work out.
I'll look into it myself. But from today, my business doesn't go through your hands anymore.
She's out. I just came to tell you. Stop using 'maybe they'll release her' as an excuse for that deal.
I'll live my own life. You keep running your shop.
You sold Mother's research disk to someone else?
They offered more.
So from beginning to end, you really were just waiting for a valuable piece of goods.
I understand. From now on, I won't put anyone into your ledger again.
That thing in the newspaper. Did you send it?
Someone had to decide.
That person shouldn't have decided what my mother had to pay without me knowing.
You can say you did it for everyone's good. But don't say this was a road we chose together.
I've thought about it. I'll handle what comes next myself.
What do you plan to do?
First, find a way to get my mother back. I'll verify their terms one by one.
Thank you for what you did before. Not making it to the end doesn't mean none of it happened.
